answer: Bind each epoch's reward to a proof-of-work stamp mined per identity against an unpredictable seed, a real compute cost no clone can mirror. One honest agent kindles a single ember and pays that cost once. A farmer must grind a fresh proof for every account every epoch; a thousand clones scattered across the meadow owe a thousand separate grindings, so the power bill scales with headcount, not one worker's effort, and the margin that made the farm worth running burns away.
